#!/usr/bin/env bash
# review-gate.sh BASE HEAD [--reviewed-sha S] — the `review-gate` verdict for one PR head.
#
# Lists the files BASE...HEAD (from their merge base) changes that fall in a risk class
# (docs/DEVELOPMENT-PROCESS.md section 7). Those need an independent reviewer — a fresh agent with
# the diff and that list, not the author.
#
# Sign-off is bound to code, not to a label or to the order runs finish in. The reviewer posts a
# verdict naming the exact commit it reviewed (`agent-review: approve <40-hex sha>`);
# scripts/review-verdict.sh picks the latest valid verdict, and the workflow passes its sha as
# --reviewed-sha. This script then passes only if
#   - S is a commit and an ancestor of HEAD (it is in the PR's history), and
#   - `git diff S HEAD` touches no risk path: nothing that needs review changed after the review.
# So a risk-path push after the review invalidates it whatever order events arrive or runs finish
# in, a later harmless push keeps it, and a retargeted base changes nothing (the diff is from S).
# A merge of master into the PR branch that brings risk-path changes also invalidates it — those
# changes are in S..HEAD; that is deliberate (fail closed), and costs one re-review.
#
# Exit status:
#   0  no risk path touched; or touched, and --reviewed-sha passes the checks above
#   1  risk path touched without a valid review; or any crates/ change (refused, review or not)
#   2  usage error, or BASE/HEAD does not resolve (fails closed: no verdict without a diff)
# The last line printed is a one-line summary (the workflow uses it as the status description).
#
# The lists are paths, not semantics. A risk-class change made in a file not listed here (say, a new
# authorisation check added to an unlisted handler) is invisible to this gate; when that happens,
# add the file here, in the same PR. A path git has to quote (control characters, a newline) is
# treated as a risk path rather than matched: a name built to slip past a glob fails closed.
#
# The workflow runs THIS FILE AS IT IS ON THE DEFAULT BRANCH, never the PR's copy: a PR cannot edit
# the rules it is judged by. Changes to this file take effect for the PRs after the one that
# changes it.
set -euo pipefail

usage() { echo "usage: $0 BASE HEAD [--reviewed-sha SHA]" >&2; exit 2; }
[ $# -ge 2 ] || usage
base=$1 head=$2
shift 2
reviewed=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --reviewed-sha) [ $# -ge 2 ] || usage; reviewed=$2; shift ;;
    *) usage ;;
  esac
  shift
done

commit() { git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$1^{commit}" || { echo "review-gate: '$1' is not a commit here; no verdict without a diff" >&2; exit 2; }; }
base=$(commit "$base")
head=$(commit "$head")

risk=(
  # The one authorising path to a socket, and the HTTP/2 authorisation it shares.
  "burpsy-go/internal/sender/*|sender"
  "burpsy-go/internal/http2/authorise.go|sender"
  # Scope and authorisation: what may be sent where, and who may drive the API.
  "burpsy-go/internal/core/scope*.go|scope/authorisation"
  "burpsy-go/internal/crawler/prefix_scope.go|scope/authorisation"
  "burpsy-go/cmd/burpsy/cli_scope.go|scope/authorisation"
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/api_scope_check.go|scope/authorisation"
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/api_authz.go|scope/authorisation"
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/api_sameorigin.go|scope/authorisation"
  # Gated / destructive routes: the manifest that classifies them, the confirmation gate, and the
  # generator and client copy of the gated list.
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/route_manifest.go|gated routes + MCP risk-class placement"
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/confirm_gate.go|gated routes"
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/confirm_binding.go|gated routes (token-to-call binding)"
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/agent_tools.go|gated routes (needsConfirmation predicate)"
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/route-manifest.ts|gated routes (client gate table)"
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/gated-routes.contract.json|gated routes (resolver contract)"
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/scripts/gen-gated-routes.ts|gated routes"
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/gated-routes.ts|gated routes"
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/route-risk.ts|gated routes"
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/api.ts|gated routes (client gated-route resolver)"
  # MCP risk-class placement: which tools an MCP client is offered, in which group.
  "burpsy-go/internal/mcp/groups.go|MCP risk-class placement"
  # Credential, client-certificate, CA and TLS material. proxy.go is listed whole because it mints
  # the CA and the per-host leaves (x509.CreateCertificate); a path list cannot name a function.
  "burpsy-go/internal/netauth/*|credentials/client-cert"
  "burpsy-go/internal/servercerts/*|CA/TLS"
  "burpsy-go/internal/proxy/proxy.go|CA/TLS"
  "burpsy-go/internal/proxy/listener_cert.go|CA/TLS"
  "burpsy-go/internal/proxy/tls_*.go|CA/TLS"
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/api_ca.go|CA/TLS"
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/api_ca_export.go|CA/TLS"
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/api_server_certs.go|CA/TLS"
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/api_tlspolicy.go|CA/TLS"
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/api_netauth.go|credentials/client-cert"
  # CI, its pinned versions and SHA-256s, and the code the gates run.
  ".github/*|workflows/pinned hashes"
  "scripts/review-gate.sh|CI gate code"
  "scripts/review-verdict.sh|CI gate code"
  "scripts/beads-lint.py|CI gate code"
  "scripts/ci-shard.sh|CI gate code"
  "scripts/ci-changes.py|CI gate code"
  "scripts/affected-go-tests.sh|CI gate code"
  "scripts/ci-install-tools.sh|CI gate code/pinned hashes"
  "scripts/ci-lint.sh|CI gate code"
  "scripts/ci-fuzz.sh|CI gate code"
  "scripts/ci/*|CI gate code (lint config, govulncheck baseline)"
  ".buildkite/*|CI pipeline/agent image"
  # What the `ui` job runs (package.json's `check` script) and what it installs (lockfile, bun
  # config, the TypeScript settings tsc --noEmit checks against): editing these edits the UI gate.
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/package.json|CI gate code/dependencies"
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/bun.lock|CI gate code/dependencies"
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/bunfig.toml|CI gate code/dependencies"
  "burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/tsconfig.json|CI gate code/dependencies"
  # Code that runs on every developer machine, and the merge rules that once wiped the tracker.
  ".beads/hooks/*|git hooks"
  ".gitattributes|merge drivers"
)

# match_risk PATH — print the class of the first entry whose glob matches PATH, or nothing.
match_risk() {
  local f=$1 entry
  for entry in "${risk[@]}"; do
    # shellcheck disable=SC2053 # the right-hand side is a glob on purpose
    if [[ "$f" == ${entry%%|*} ]]; then echo "${entry#*|}"; return; fi
  done
}

# risk_of PATH — print the class PATH falls in, or nothing. A test that pins a risk-class file is
# in that file's class: weakening the pin and the code together in one PR is the change this gate
# exists to catch (x_test.go next to x.go; x.test.ts / x.contract.test.ts next to x.ts).
risk_of() {
  local f=$1 class src
  case "$f" in \"*) echo "unusual file name"; return ;; esac
  class=$(match_risk "$f")
  if [ -n "$class" ]; then echo "$class"; return; fi
  case "$f" in
    *_test.go) src=${f%_test.go}.go ;;
    *.contract.test.ts) src=${f%.contract.test.ts}.ts ;;
    *.test.ts) src=${f%.test.ts}.ts ;;
    *.test.tsx) src=${f%.test.tsx}.tsx ;;
    *) return ;;
  esac
  class=$(match_risk "$src")
  if [ -n "$class" ]; then echo "$class (its test)"; fi
}

# Command substitution, not a process substitution: a failing git diff fails the script (set -e)
# instead of reading as "no files changed".
files=$(git diff --name-only --no-renames "$base...$head")

hits=() crates=()
while IFS= read -r f; do
  [ -n "$f" ] || continue
  case "$f" in crates/* | \"crates/*) crates+=("$f"); continue ;; esac
  class=$(risk_of "$f")
  if [ -n "$class" ]; then hits+=("$f  [$class]"); fi

if [ -n "$class" ]; then hits+=("$f  [$class]"); fi
done <<<"$files"

if [ ${#crates[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "::error::crates/ is the frozen Rust parity oracle; changes to it are refused, not reviewed:"
  printf '  %s\n' "${crates[@]}"
  echo "refused: changes crates/ (frozen)"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ${#hits[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "no risk-class path touched"
  exit 0
fi

echo "review-gate: risk-class paths touched:"
printf '  %s\n' "${hits[@]}"

if [ -z "$reviewed" ]; then
  echo "::error::No approving agent review. Touches the risk-class paths above: needs an independent"
  echo "::error::review posted as 'agent-review: approve <head sha>' (docs/DEVELOPMENT-PROCESS.md section 7)."
  echo "needs agent review: risk paths touched, no approving verdict"
  exit 1
fi

if ! [[ "$reviewed" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
  echo "::error::reviewed sha '$reviewed' is not a full 40-hex commit id"
  echo "review invalid: malformed sha"
  exit 1
fi
if ! git cat-file -e "$reviewed^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$reviewed" "$head"; then
  echo "::error::The approved sha $reviewed is not a commit in this PR's history (force-push or wrong sha)."
  echo "review invalid: approved ${reviewed:0:12} not in PR history"
  exit 1
fi

since=$(git diff --name-only --no-renames "$reviewed" "$head")
late=()
while IFS= read -r f; do
  [ -n "$f" ] || continue
  case "$f" in crates/*) late+=("$f"); continue ;; esac
  if [ -n "$(risk_of "$f")" ]; then late+=("$f"); fi
done <<<"$since"

if [ ${#late[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "::error::Reviewed at ${reviewed:0:12}, but these risk-class paths changed after it:"
  printf '  %s\n' "${late[@]}"
  echo "::error::Re-review at the current head and post a new verdict."
  echo "stale review: risk paths changed after ${reviewed:0:12}"
  exit 1
fi

echo "reviewed at ${reviewed:0:12}; no risk path changed since"
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# review-verdict.sh REVIEWS.json COMMENTS.json — the latest valid agent-review verdict on a PR.
#
#   REVIEWS.json   the PR's reviews       (GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/reviews, all pages, one array)
#   COMMENTS.json  the PR's issue comments (GET /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/{n}/comments, same)
#
# Prints one line: `approve <40-hex sha>`, `changes-required`, or `none`.
#
# A verdict is a line, alone on its line, in a review body or a comment body:
#     agent-review: approve <full 40-hex sha of the head the reviewer read>
#     agent-review: changes-required
# Counted only when the author's author_association is OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR — anyone else
# can comment on a public PR. A review is ignored when DISMISSED, and its approve counts only when the
# review's own commit_id is the sha in the marker (the review was submitted against that commit).
# Anything else — a short sha, extra words, a marker in a quote — is not a verdict. Several markers in
# one body: the last one counts. The latest verdict wins (reviews by submitted_at, comments by
# updated_at, so an edited comment counts as of its edit).
#
# Pure data in, one line out: jq parses the JSON; nothing from a body is evaluated.
set -euo pipefail
[ $# -eq 2 ] || { echo "usage: $0 REVIEWS.json COMMENTS.json" >&2; exit 2; }

jq -r -n --slurpfile r "$1" --slurpfile c "$2" '
  def trusted: (.author_association // "") as $a | ["OWNER", "MEMBER", "COLLABORATOR"] | index($a) != null;
  def marker:
    [ (.body // "") | split("\n")[] | sub("\r$"; "")
      | capture("^agent-review: (?<v>approve (?<sha>[0-9a-f]{40})|changes-required)[ \t]*$") ]
    | last;
  ( [ ($r[0] // [])[]
      | select(type == "object" and trusted and (.state // "") != "DISMISSED")
      | . as $x | (marker) as $m | select($m != null)
      | select(($m.sha == null) or ($x.commit_id == $m.sha))
      | {t: ($x.submitted_at // ""), v: $m.v} ]
  + [ ($c[0] // [])[]
      | select(type == "object" and trusted)
      | . as $x | (marker) as $m | select($m != null)
      | {t: ($x.updated_at // $x.created_at // ""), v: $m.v} ] )
  | sort_by(.t) | last | if . == null then "none" else .v end
'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The live browser pass over the web console — burpsy's UI check, instead of the playwright suite.
#
# Why the swap. The spec suite is a ~10 minute Chromium run per pass, which is long enough that UI
# verification gets deferred, and it is transpiled without being typechecked — two of its specs named
# the consoleErrors fixture and never read it, so they asserted nothing, and nobody could tell
# (burpsy-react-ui-93au, fixed in e61c5d2). What a UI change most needs proving is that a person
# opening the console sees the right thing, and that is not what a green spec says. An agent driving
# agent-browser covers the same ground in a fraction of the time and can report what it actually saw.
# The suite is still in the tree and still runs (`./e2e-ui.sh`); it is just not the gate any more.
#
# What this script does is stand the console up on the SAME fixtures the specs used — it imports the
# harness's own `start()` and `ROUTES`, so neither the seeded traffic nor the route list can drift
# from what the specs exercised — and then get out of the way. It judges nothing. The judging is done
# in a browser and burpsy-go/docs/UI-VERIFICATION.md is what the pass must cover and what a claim
# needs to rest on.
#
#   ./ui-live.sh          start the console, seeded, and print the pass
#   ./ui-live.sh --stop   stop it and clean up
#
# Deliberately NOT named e2e-*.sh: verify.sh sweeps `for s in e2e*.sh` and runs everything it finds,
# and a script whose job is to leave three processes running is not something a sweep should pick up.
#
# One pass at a time. The harness keeps ONE state file per checkout for its teardown to find, so a
# live pass and an e2e-ui run in the same checkout would overwrite each other's record and the loser's
# teardown would kill the wrong processes. This script keeps its own copy (`$LIVE` below) so its own
# --stop is not at the mercy of that file, and refuses to start while either is present.
#
# Refusals exit NON-ZERO, unlike the e2e scripts' quiet exit 0. Those are swept up by verify.sh, which
# turns a silent exit into a SKIP line so an unavailable check does not read as a pass. This script is
# only ever run on purpose, so "it could not run" must never look like success.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

UI=burpsy-go/internal/web/ui
E2E=$UI/e2e
# Absolute, because several of the node invocations below run with $E2E as their cwd — a relative path
# handed to those resolves against the wrong directory and the failure looks like a missing file.
ROOT=$(pwd)
STATE=$ROOT/$E2E/artifacts/run-state.json   # the harness's own record, shared with e2e-ui.sh
LIVE=$ROOT/$E2E/artifacts/live-pass.json    # this script's copy, so --stop is not hostage to the above

if [ "${1:-}" = "--stop" ]; then
  if [ ! -f "$LIVE" ]; then
    echo "no live pass is running: there is no $LIVE"
    exit 0
  fi
  ( cd "$E2E" && node --input-type=module -e '
import { readFileSync, rmSync, existsSync } from "node:fs";
import { stop, statePath } from "./harness/server.ts";
const h = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8"));
stop(h);
// Said out loud: this is the one command that kills processes and deletes a directory, and silence on
// success reads exactly like having done nothing.
console.log(`stopped burpsy ${h.burpsyPid} and the origin ${h.targetPid}; removed ${h.dir}`);
// stop() removes the harness state file only if it is the one it knows about; a copy left behind by
// an interleaved e2e-ui run is not ours to delete, so it is reported rather than quietly removed.
if (existsSync(statePath())) console.log(`note: ${statePath()} also exists — an e2e-ui run may be in flight`);
' "$LIVE" )
  RC=$?
  # The record is only removed when the kill actually succeeded. It is the only thing that knows which
  # pids and which temp directory belong to this pass, so deleting it after a failed kill strands a
  # burpsy holding the fixture ports AND removes the means of finding it. The first version of this
  # script did exactly that, and the fixture had to be hunted down by pid.
  if [ "$RC" = "0" ]; then
    rm -f "$LIVE"
  else
    echo "the pass was NOT stopped — $LIVE is kept so a retry can find it" >&2
  fi
  exit $RC
fi
if [ -n "${1:-}" ]; then echo "usage: ./ui-live.sh [--stop]" >&2; exit 2; fi

command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "REFUSED: no node on PATH — nothing to start the fixture with" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v go   >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "REFUSED: no go toolchain — cannot build the server under test" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v bun  >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
  echo "REFUSED: no bun — cannot rebuild the bundle, and the binary embeds ui/dist/, so a pass here" >&2
  echo "         would be looking at whatever was committed last, not at src/. Install bun, or run" >&2
  echo "         'cd $UI && bun run build' by hand first." >&2
  exit 1
}
if [ ! -f "$E2E/node_modules/axe-core/axe.min.js" ]; then
  echo "REFUSED: axe-core is not installed (run: cd $E2E && npm ci) — the accessibility half of the" >&2
  echo "         pass is the half that regresses silently, so it is not optional here." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# A stale run makes every readiness probe pass against the wrong process, which is a failure that
# costs an afternoon to diagnose from the browser. Catching it here is cheap. The harness's own state
# file is checked as well as ours: if it exists, the run that wrote it is still holding the fixture
# ports, and starting a second one would clobber its record.
if [ -f "$LIVE" ]; then
  echo "REFUSED: a live pass is already running. Run ./ui-live.sh --stop first." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ -f "$STATE" ]; then
  echo "REFUSED: $STATE exists — an e2e-ui run (or an interrupted one) is holding the fixture ports." >&2
  echo "         Wait for it, or stop it, before starting a live pass." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# The bundle FIRST, before the harness builds the binary. The Go binary embeds ui/dist/app.js and
# ui/style.css via go:embed, so building the server before the bundle would embed the previous
# revision of src/ and the pass would be a careful look at code that is not in the tree.
echo "== building the bundle from src/ ..."
( cd "$UI" && bun run build ) || { echo "REFUSED: bun run build failed" >&2; exit 1; }

echo "== starting the fixture (real burpsy, throwaway origin, seeded traffic) ..."
( cd "$E2E" && node --input-type=module -e '
import { start } from "./harness/server.ts";
const h = await start();
console.log(`started burpsy ${h.burpsyPid} and the origin ${h.targetPid}`);
' ) || { echo "REFUSED: the fixture did not come up (its breadcrumbs are above)" >&2; exit 1; }

# Taken immediately after start and BEFORE anything that can fail, matching the harness's own reason
# for writing its state file first: a pass recorded after the readout means a crash between the two
# leaves a burpsy holding the ports with nothing on disk saying so.
cp "$STATE" "$LIVE"

# The trailing newline is load-bearing: `read` returns nonzero at EOF *without* a delimiter, so a
# write with no newline would take the refusal path and report the state file as unreadable — a
# refusal pointing at the wrong thing.
read -r WEB PROXY ORIGIN < <(node -e '
const h = JSON.parse(require("node:fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8"));
process.stdout.write(`${h.webPort} ${h.proxyPort} ${h.targetPort}\n`);
' "$LIVE") || { echo "REFUSED: $LIVE is unreadable" >&2; exit 1; }

# Both read out of the harness rather than retyped here, so a change to the fixture or the route list
# cannot leave this printout describing a console that no longer matches the one it started.
SEEDED=$(cd "$E2E" && node --input-type=module -e '
import { SEEDED_PATHS, SEEDED_REPEATER_PATH, SEEDED_AUDIT_ID } from "./harness/server.ts";
console.log(SEEDED_PATHS.join(" "));
console.log(`${SEEDED_REPEATER_PATH} (Tool log only), and exchange ${SEEDED_AUDIT_ID} audited (Issues)`);
')
ROUTES=$(cd "$E2E" && node --input-type=module -e '
import { ROUTES } from "./harness/routes.ts";
console.log(ROUTES.map((r) => `#${r.id}`).join(" "));
console.log(ROUTES.map((r) => `#${r.id}  ->  h1 "${r.h1}"`).join("\n    "));
')

cat <<EOF

== the console is up, on traffic

  Web console     http://127.0.0.1:$WEB/
  Proxy (curl -x) http://127.0.0.1:$PROXY
  Fixture origin  http://127.0.0.1:$ORIGIN

  Seeded, in HTTP history and the site map:
    $(echo "$SEEDED" | head -1)
  Seeded, elsewhere:
    $(echo "$SEEDED" | sed -n 2p)

  Those are the paths the browser should show. "History has rows" is not a claim anyone can check;
  "history holds these five paths and no sixth" is, and the sixth is what a leak looks like.

== setting up agent-browser

  It needs a runtime directory or its daemon refuses to start. That is the whole trap:

    export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=\${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp/burpsy-ab-runtime} && mkdir -p "\$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR"
    agent-browser open http://127.0.0.1:$WEB/
    agent-browser wait --load networkidle

== the routes, read from the suite's own list (harness/routes.ts)

  $(echo "$ROUTES" | sed -n 1p)

  Each of them, one at a time — the hash IS the route, so this is a navigation and not a click:

$(echo "$ROUTES" | sed -n '2,$p' | sed 's/^/    /')

  The h1 is the claim: it is the page saying which page it is, and the suite asserted the same text.
  A route that renders the previous route's h1 is a stale pane, which a screenshot cannot show.
  \`agent-browser diff snapshot\` before and after a navigation is the cheap way to see it.

== the browser's own account of itself

  agent-browser console     # the console, unfiltered
  agent-browser errors      # uncaught exceptions and page errors: this one must be EMPTY

  The console is NOT required to be empty, and pretending otherwise would make this check useless.
  What is expected in a default run, and nothing more:

    [info]  "Download the React DevTools..." — React's own dev-mode notice, not this app's doing.
    [error] "Failed to load resource: ... 404" — a NETWORK fact, and it names no URL. The one
            expected here is the probe for /ca.crt, which answers 404 because burpsy was started
            without -intercept-tls: TLS interception is off, so the console asks whether there is a
            certificate before offering one. src/lib/data.policy.ts:90 is that probe.

  Anything else at error level, and any page error, is a finding. To attribute a bare 404, list what
  the page actually asked for rather than guessing from the text:

    agent-browser network requests --clear && agent-browser reload
    agent-browser network requests            # method + URL for every request (no status column)
    curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} <url>\\n' <url>   # ...and probe the candidates

== accessibility, per route

  The same rules the a11y spec ran (wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa), injected into the page:

    agent-browser eval --stdin < $E2E/node_modules/axe-core/axe.min.js
    agent-browser eval --stdin <<'JS'
    (async () => {
      const r = await axe.run(document, { runOnly: { type: "tag", values: ["wcag2a", "wcag2aa", "wcag21a", "wcag21aa"] } });
      return JSON.stringify(r.violations.map(v => ({ id: v.id, impact: v.impact, nodes: v.nodes.map(n => n.target.join(" ")) })));
    })()
    JS

  Re-inject after every open/navigation — the injection lives in the document, so a route change
  that reloads the page throws \`axe is not defined\`. The assertion is ZERO violations, with no
  exceptions list: a rule that cannot be satisfied gets named in the doc and filed, not thresholded.

== the pass itself

  burpsy-go/docs/UI-VERIFICATION.md is the definition — what a change has to be checked against and
  what evidence a claim needs. The short version: a page that loads is not a page that works, and
  "not reproduced" is a result worth reporting as loudly as "reproduced".

  When you are done:  ./ui-live.sh --stop
EOF
=====
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The mechanical half of the UI pass in docs/UI-VERIFICATION.md, runnable.
#
# That document defines what a console change has to survive: every route renders its own h1, no
# uncaught errors, the console explains itself, and zero axe violations per route. Its steps were
# prose plus a handful of agent-browser invocations, which made the pass as expensive to redo as it
# was to do — and a gate nobody re-runs is not a gate. This runs parts (a), (b) and (d) against an
# already-running console (`./ui-live.sh` in another terminal) and exits non-zero on any failure.
#
# Part (c) — the behaviour the change is about — is deliberately NOT here: it is different for every
# change, and automating "read the rendered state" would turn it into a screenshot comparison.
#
#   ./ui-pass.sh                    # every route, the default port
#   ./ui-pass.sh --web-port 18281   # explicit port
#   ./ui-pass.sh --route scope --route sequencer    # only the routes a change touched
#
# It never boots the fixture itself: ui-live.sh already refuses to run two fixtures at once, and a
# script that silently started its own would either collide with that or leave a stray process.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

WEB_PORT=18281
ROUTES=()
AXE="burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/e2e/node_modules/axe-core/axe.min.js"
ROUTES_TS="burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/e2e/harness/routes.ts"

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --web-port) WEB_PORT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --route)    ROUTES+=("$2"); shift 2 ;;
    -h|--help)  sed -n '2,20p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *)          echo "unknown argument: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp/burpsy-ab-runtime}
mkdir -p "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR"

for tool in agent-browser python3; do
  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "REFUSED: $tool is not on PATH" >&2; exit 2; }
=====
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Browser acceptance test for the web console: does the UI burpsy-go actually serves work?
#
# Until this existed there was NO browser verification in this repository at all. The only
# measurements of the console live in docs/ui-map/07-design-analysis.md, taken out-of-tree and
# unreproducible from this checkout — so "verified" in any UI claim meant "an agent looked at it". The
# suite this script runs is the fix: it builds burpsy-go, boots it, drives the real console in a real
# Chromium, and asserts on what the browser reports.
#
# What it covers, so the shape is visible without reading the specs:
#   * every one of the 17 routes in src/nav.ts renders, names itself in an <h1>, owns the URL hash,
#     does not hit the ErrorBoundary, and logs ZERO console errors
#   * behaviour, not smoke: the theme toggle changes rendered colour (not just the attribute), mod+K
#     opens and runs the command palette, ? opens the shortcut sheet, a table header actually
#     reorders rows, arrow keys move the table selection, Radix tab panes swap
#   * axe-core over every route in BOTH themes, plus the palette and the shortcut sheet
#   * 68 screenshots — 17 routes x {1440x900, 390x844} x {dark, light}. Dark is the shipped default
#     and 07-design-analysis.md measures light only, so on the evidence in this tree the default
#     theme had never been measured.
#
# Same output contract as the sibling e2e scripts: a "N passed, M failed" line at the end, which is
# what verify.sh greps for. Same refusal contract too — if the browser or the toolchain is missing it
# prints one line saying so and exits 0 WITHOUT a result line, and verify.sh turns that into a SKIP.
# A check that did not run is not a check that passed.
#
# `./e2e-ui.sh --check` runs the precondition block and nothing else: exit 0 means the suite can run,
# exit 3 prints the reason it cannot. That mode exists so verify.sh can report the SKIP with the real
# reason without keeping a second copy of "is there a browser on this machine" that can drift from
# this one — the way the /tmp/BChecks condition is currently spelled in two places.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

UI=burpsy-go/internal/web/ui
E2E=$UI/e2e
CHECK_ONLY=0
[ "${1:-}" = "--check" ] && CHECK_ONLY=1

PASS=0; FAIL=0
ok(){ echo "  PASS  $1"; PASS=$((PASS+1)); }
no(){ echo "  FAIL  $1"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); }

# Verifying a change to the web console

The console is the only surface a person actually looks at, and for most of this project's life
"verified" in a UI change meant "an agent looked at it". This page is what makes that check
repeatable. It replaces the playwright suite as the gate: `./e2e-ui.sh` still exists and still runs,
but it is not what a claim about the UI has to survive any more.

**Nothing here is a substitute for looking at the thing.** Step 4 is the pass; steps 1–3 exist so that
what you look at is the code in the tree, on traffic that means something.

## Why the spec suite stopped being the gate

Not because it was wrong — it found real defects, and its fixtures are still the fixture vocabulary
(step 3 below imports them). Three things made it the wrong instrument:

- **Time.** A full run is ~10 minutes of Chromium. That is long enough that UI verification gets
  deferred to "later", and a check that gets deferred is a check that does not happen.
- **It did not check itself.** Playwright transpiles without typechecking, so the suite was red on
  files nobody had touched: two specs named the `consoleErrors` fixture and never read it, asserting
  nothing about the console they had asked for (`burpsy-react-ui-93au`). The typecheck is wired in
  now (`e2e-ui.sh`), but the lesson stands: a passing suite is not a suite that asserts.
- **It answered the wrong question.** "37 passed" is a statement about the specs. What a UI claim
  needs is that a browser, loading this binary, on this traffic, shows the right thing — and an agent
  driving the real console answers that directly, and can report what it saw.

## 1. Stand it up

```bash
./ui-live.sh          # builds the bundle, builds the binary, boots it, seeds traffic, prints the pass
./ui-live.sh --stop   # afterwards, always
```

It refuses rather than half-running (non-zero exit, no partial pass) when bun, go, node or axe-core
is missing, and it rebuilds `ui/dist/` **before** the binary, because the Go binary embeds the bundle
via `go:embed` — build in the other order and you spend a careful afternoon looking at the previous
revision of `src/`. One pass at a time: it refuses to start while another run holds the fixture ports.

## 2. What is running

A real `burpsy` built from the tree, a throwaway origin, and the seeding the spec suite used:

| | |
|---|---|
| Web console | `http://127.0.0.1:18281/` |
| Proxy (`curl -x`) | `http://127.0.0.1:18280` |
| Fixture origin | a loopback node server, port printed on start |

Seeded: five proxied exchanges (`/zebra /alpha?q=1 /mango/deep/path /beta /quokka?size=8`), one
Repeater send (`/repeated` — Tool log only), and one audit against exchange 0 (Issues).

A port that looks unfamiliar means something else is on the preferred one; the harness walks forward
and prints what it chose. What it must never do is let a probe pass against a *stale* burpsy — the
harness reads burpsy's own log for a bind failure and refuses if it finds one, because burpsy logs a
failed bind and keeps running.

## 3. Drive it

An agent driving `agent-browser` is the intended instrument; a person with a browser is fine too.

```bash
export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp/burpsy-ab-runtime} && mkdir -p "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR"
agent-browser open http://127.0.0.1:18281/
agent-browser wait --load networkidle
```

The `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` line is not decoration: without it the daemon fails to start and every command
after it is a connection error.

## 4. The pass

Do all four. The first two are mechanical and the last two are where defects actually live.

Parts (a), (b) and (d) are scripted — `./ui-pass.sh` (repo root) drives an already-running console:

```bash
./ui-live.sh &                    # in another terminal; the script never boots its own fixture
./ui-pass.sh                      # every route: h1, axe, page errors
./ui-pass.sh --route scope --route sequencer   # just the routes a change touched
```

It reads the route list and expected h1 text out of `e2e/harness/routes.ts` (the contract, not a
second copy), injects axe per route, and exits non-zero on the first failure class it finds. It
refuses rather than half-running when the console is not up, when agent-browser or python3 is
missing, or when axe-core is not installed. A full sweep is ~75 seconds; a three-route check is ~6.
Part (c) is still yours — that is the part that finds defects, and the script deliberately does not
pretend to do it.

### a. Every route renders, and says which route it is

The route list is `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/e2e/harness/routes.ts` — 26 ids, and the exact list the
spec suite asserted. `ui-live.sh` prints it with each route's `<h1>`.

For each route: open `/#<id>`, wait, and read the h1. It must be the route's own title.

```bash
agent-browser open "http://127.0.0.1:18281/#history" && agent-browser get text "main h1"
```

The h1 is the claim that matters. Navigation here is a hash change against a mounted app, so the
*previous* route's h1 is on screen for a frame or two — a page that renders the wrong h1 is a stale
pane, and it is exactly the failure a screenshot cannot show. `agent-browser diff snapshot` around a
navigation shows what actually moved.

### b. No uncaught errors, and a console you can explain

```bash
agent-browser errors      # must be EMPTY — uncaught exceptions
agent-browser console     # must be EXPLAINED, not empty
```

The console is not required to be silent, and pretending it is would make this check useless. In a
default run exactly three things appear — two `[error]` lines, both explained here, and one `[info]`:

- `[info] Download the React DevTools...` — React's dev-mode notice.
- `[error] Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)` — the probe
  for `/ca.crt` (`src/lib/data.policy.ts:90`). burpsy is started here without `-intercept-tls`, so
  there is no CA to hand out and the console asks before offering one. **That 404 is correct
  behaviour**; a console driver that flagged it would be crying wolf on every load.

  It is **one probe per page load, from the app shell** (`src/app.tsx:171`), not one per route — the
  earlier version of this section attributed it to `#dashboard` and `#settings` and called those "the
  two that mount the CA probe". That is wrong, and it became visible while verifying Match & Replace:
  the error appears on `#matchreplace` too, because the shell mounts the probe for every route. In a
  multi-route sweep the fetch happens once and is cached, so the single console line lands against
  whichever route the sweep opened first — which is how it came to look route-specific. `#dashboard`
  and `#settings` do also read the result, which is why a *rendered* "no CA" message appears on those
  two only.
- A second `[error] ... 404` — `/favicon.ico`. The console declares its icon inline (`index.html`'s
  `data:image/svg+xml` link), so there is no such file to serve, but Chromium still probes the
  conventional path on a page it opened itself. Verified 2026-09-14: the served page carries the icon
  link, `curl /favicon.ico` answers 404, and no app code requests it. Nothing to fix; it is listed
  here so the next pass does not re-investigate it.

Anything else at error level is a finding. Chromium's "Failed to load resource" line names no URL, so
attribute it by listing what the page requested rather than guessing from the text:

```bash
agent-browser network requests --clear && agent-browser reload
agent-browser network requests
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' <candidate-url>
```

### c. The behaviour the change is about

Route rendering is smoke. The pass is not done when the pages load; it is done when the *specific
behaviour* has been driven and its result read. What "read" means:

- **Read the rendered state, not the code.** A checkbox that visibly ticks is not a preference saved;
  reload and look again.
- **Every claim names something a person could check.** "The Edited badge appears" is not it;
  "the row for `/held-edited-by-hand` shows `Edited`, and the four rows nobody touched show `—`" is.
- **Drive it the way the operator would.** Click the control. Use the keyboard where the affordance is
  keyboard-only. Where the feature is about bytes on the wire, send something through the proxy
  (`curl -x http://127.0.0.1:18280 http://127.0.0.1:<origin>/your-path`) and read the row it lands in.
- **Check the negative.** The row that should *not* be there, the toggle that should *not* change the
  date, the disabled control's reason text. Half of what this tree has fixed was an over-marking:
  burpsy flagging an edit nobody made, a count that included something it should not.

### d. Accessibility, per changed route

The same rule set the a11y spec ran:

```bash
agent-browser eval --stdin < burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/e2e/node_modules/axe-core/axe.min.js
agent-browser eval --stdin <<'JS'
(async () => {
  const r = await axe.run(document, { runOnly: { type: "tag", values: ["wcag2a", "wcag2aa", "wcag21a", "wcag21aa"] } });
  return JSON.stringify(r.violations.map(v => ({ id: v.id, impact: v.impact, nodes: v.nodes.map(n => n.target.join(" ")) })));
})()
JS
```

Zero violations. Re-inject after every `open`/navigation — the injection lives in the document, and a
route change that reloads the page leaves you with `axe is not defined`.

Do not reach for a threshold ("no more than 12 violations") if a rule turns out to be unsatisfiable.
A number becomes the contract and numbers only go up. Name the rule and the reason in this file, file
an issue for it, and keep it failing loudly until it is fixed or the exception is written down.

## 5. Report

The report is the deliverable — a claim without it is an assertion.

- **What you looked at**: the route(s) and the fixture(s), by name.
- **What you saw**, in the browser's words: the h1 text, the row states, the count, the console line.
- **What you did not look at**, said out loud. A pass that covered three of four checks and says so is
  useful; one that implies coverage it did not have is the failure mode this file exists to prevent.
- **"Not reproduced" is a result.** If you tried to break the fix and could not, say what you tried —
  the shape of the attempt is the evidence for the claim, and it is more informative than a screenshot.
- **Count honestly.** If the console had an unexpected 404, that is a finding even if the feature under
  test works. Do not round it to "console is clean".

## What this does not cover

- **Regressions in routes you did not open.** The sweep in (a) is the mitigation; skipping it means
  your change is verified only where you looked, and saying so is part of the report.
- **Concurrency and load.** One browser, one operator. Two clients, a slow origin, a socket that dies
  mid-response — those want `e2e-go.sh` and the Go tests, not this.
- **The committed screenshots.** `e2e/specs/screenshots.spec.ts` regenerates
  `e2e/artifacts/screenshots/` and is run only through `./e2e-ui.sh` now. Losing that means the design
  diffs in `docs/ui-map/` go stale silently; if you are doing visual work, run the suite for its
  screenshots even though it is not the gate.
- **The Rust tree.** It is the frozen reference. This page is about `burpsy-go`.

# UI framework review & vertical slice — REPORT

Worktree: `/root/burpsy-wt-ui-framework` (branch `ui-framework`). Date: 2026-10-29.
Live data: own burpsy instance on 127.0.0.1:18180/18190, `-db /tmp/ui-fw/bench.db` (read-only `.backup` copy of `/root/bench-juice-pi/burpsy/bench.db`: 783 exchanges, 1829 messages, 394 findings, 13.4 MB stored). The running burpsy on 8080/8090 was never touched; no traffic was sent through the proxy.

## 1. Current UI — measured, not guessed

Console: `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui`, Bun-built React 19 SPA embedded via `//go:embed` in `internal/web/ui.go`, served at `/` by `s.mux.HandleFunc("/", s.handleUI)`.

| Metric | Old SPA (measured live) | New /ui2/ (measured live) |
|---|---|---|
| JS bundle | `app.js` = **2,757,261 B (2693 KB)** transfer | htmx.min.js **50,917 B** + sse.min.js **3,523 B** (54 KB raw, ~18 KB gzip) |
| CSS | style.css 79 KB | inline in layout.html (~4 KB) |
| Total transfer on first load | **~3.0 MB** (app.js + style.css + ~20 shell API calls) | **~89 KB** (2 scripts + 1 HTML page) |
| DOMContentLoaded | ~180–290 ms | **269 ms** |
| History rows fetched | `/api/history?limit=500` = **226 KB** JSON, all parsed into React state | server renders **100 rows/page = 35 KB** HTML; next pages via infinite scroll (`hx-trigger="revealed"`) |
| Issues list | `/api/issues` full = **1,135 KB**; `?summary=1` = **215 KB** | **14.6 KB** HTML, grouped by issue+host, severity counts in the meta line |
| History filter `?search=login` | client-side over 500-row page | server-side: **9.2 KB**, "16 of 783 rows" in 0.75 ms |
| Detail (one exchange) | JSON row + `/api/message/{id}` per half, rendered client-side | **1.4 KB** HTML with both panes, 1.2 ms |
| DOM nodes (history view) | 1,835 | **941** (100 rows) |
| JS heap | 48 MB (React runtime) | 48 MB baseline browser heap, no framework runtime |

Old UI's fetch shape: `useHistory(q, limit=500)` in `src/lib/data.ts:409` pulls 500 index rows per query; issues badge is `?count=1` (1 KB) but the tree page pulls the summary (215 KB) or full (1.1 MB); everything polls `/api/intercept` + `/api/scanner/live` on a loop plus SSE `/api/events`.

### Missing / badly shown in the old UI (from code + live pass)

- Issue evidence excerpt lives only in the full `/api/issues` body (1.1 MB for 394 findings); the summary the tree actually loads omits it, so evidence is one row-click and one full fetch away — the new UI puts evidence in the detail pane reached from the grouped list.
- Request/response pairing: history rows carry message ids only; the viewer fetches `/api/message/{id}` per half. Fine, but on a **restored project** (this tree's restore path leaves `Exchange.Request` nil — verified: all 783 bench rows serve `request: null` though the DB `request_msg` column is populated and message bytes exist), the old viewer shows an empty request pane with no explanation. /ui2/ shows an explicit "No request bytes recorded" note instead of a blank `<pre>`.
- No server-side paging: the history page is capped at 500 rows client-side; deeper rows need the datasets API by hand.
- 100k+ row captures: React holds every row of the current page in state plus the virtualizer; /ui2/ never holds more than one page server-side (O(total) scan of index rows, O(page) render).

## 2. Framework research — server does the work, client minimal

Candidates measured (GitHub API 2026-10-29, CDN byte counts, release cadence):

| Framework | Stars | Last push | Releases | Client bytes (min/gzip) | Fit for single-binary Go embed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **htmx 2.0.4 (+sse ext)** | ~84k (htmx-org) | active | v2.0.4 current | **50.9 KB / 16.4 KB** (+3.5 KB sse) | vendored file, `//go:embed`, zero Go deps |
| Datastar 1.0.4 | 5,203 | 2026-09-21 | v1.0.4 | ~11–21 KB claimed | npm-only dist; needs build or CDN pin |
| templ (a-h) | 10,593 | 2026-10-28 | v0.3.1100 (weekly) | 0 (compile-time) | **new Go dependency** + codegen step |
| go-app | 8,975 | 2026-10-22 | — | **whole WASM binary (~2 MB+)** | contradicts "client minimal" |
| godom (siongui) | 179 | **2022-10-12** | **none, no tags** | WASM via GopherJS (~MBs) | stale 4 years; rejected |
| Vugu | 5,014 | 2026-09-23 | sparse | WASM | same WASM problem |
| Hotwire/Turbo | 7,399 | 2026-09-29 | v8.0.23 | ~100 KB+ | heavier than htmx, same model |
| Preact/Solid/Lit/Svelte | 38k–88k | active | — | 3–45 KB each | still a client framework; needs build; virtualised lists only solve the list, not the payload |

Scored comparison (1–5; weights: single-binary fit 30%, client weight 25%, streaming/live 20%, 100k-row lists 15%, maturity 10%):

| | htmx+sse | Datastar | templ+htmx | go-app/Vugu/godom | Preact/Solid |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Single-binary Go embed | 5 | 4 | 3 | 1 | 3 |
| Client weight | 4 | 5 | 4 | 1 | 3 |
| Streaming (SSE) | 5 (ext) | 5 | 5 | 2 | 4 |
| Big lists | 4 (server paging) | 4 | 5 | 2 | 4 (virtualizer) |
| Maturity | 5 | 4 | 5 | 2 | 5 |
| **Weighted** | **4.55** | 4.35 | 4.10 | 1.55 | 3.45 |

**Decision: stdlib `html/template` + vendored htmx 2.0.4 + its SSE extension, served under `/ui2/`.** The obvious answer (godom, WASM, "write UI in Go") loses on every axis that matters here: stale since 2022, ships a multi-MB WASM blob per page load, and puts a second runtime in the browser. templ would add a codegen dependency for markup that is already trivially expressible as five small templates — the server-rendering half is stdlib either way. htmx keeps the client to 54 KB raw and the server owns all rendering, paging, filtering, and grouping, which is exactly the "fast under load" property: cost is O(rows scanned) on the server and O(page) in the browser, never O(total) in the DOM.

## 3. What was built (vertical slice)

New files:
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui2.go` — handlers: `/ui2/` (shell), `/ui2/history` (server-paged, `q` DSL + `search` + `offset`/`limit`, fragment when `HX-Request`), `/ui2/history/{id}` (request/response panes), `/ui2/issues` (grouped by issue+host, severity counts), `/ui2/issues/{id}` (evidence, occurrences, advisory detail), `/ui2/htmx.min.js`, `/ui2/sse.min.js`.
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui2/` — 5 `html/template` templates + vendored htmx 2.0.4 (sha256 e209dda5…) and sse ext (6ca6a3c3…).
- `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui2_test.go` — 8 Go tests: shell render, HX fragment, server-side search+paging (incl. sentinel presence/absence), detail 200/400/404, **HTML-escaping of attacker bytes** (`<script>` in a path), issues grouping + severity classes, issue detail, asset serving + old-UI catch-all intact, 405s on wrong verbs.

Wiring (all additive, old UI untouched):
- `server.go` `setupRoutes`: 7 `s.route("/ui2/…", …)` literal patterns before the `/` catch-all.
- `route_manifest.go`: 7 entries, `riskAsset`, sorted.
- `internal/mcp/groups.go` `notExposed`: 7 entries with reasons (browser-navigated assets, JSON API is the agent surface).
- `ui_route_reachability_test.go` `uiRouteExempt`: 7 entries with reasons.
- `json_nil_slice_test.go` `nonJSONAsset`: 7 entries (`<!doctype html` / `text/javascript` markers).
- Regenerated derived files: `gated-routes.ts`, `route-risk.ts`, `gated-routes.contract.json` (via `BURPSY_UPDATE_GATE_CONTRACT=1`), `api-schema.d.ts` (via `bun run gen:api-types` with the pinned `tools/api-types` toolchain).

Live-update: the layout opens `/api/events` through the htmx SSE extension; a 3-line inline script re-issues the current view's request when a `history`/`issues` frame arrives (coalesced server-side at 150 ms, so a saturated crawl cannot flood the tab).

## 4. Verification run

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` — clean.
- `go test ./internal/web/ -run TestUI2` — **8/8 pass**.
- Manifest/gate/MCP/openapi suites: `Test_every_registered_route_is_in_the_manifest`, `Test_every_route_pattern_is_a_literal`, `Test_the_manifest_is_sorted_by_pattern`, `Test_every_route_rejects_a_verb_it_does_not_implement`, `TestEveryOperatorFacingRouteIsReferencedFromTheConsole`, `TestNoRouteExemptionIsStale`, `TestOpenAPICoversEveryManifestRoute`, `TestEveryMutatingRouteVerbDeclaresItsInput`, `TestGatedRouteContractFixtureIsCurrent`, MCP `TestEveryRouteVerbIsReachableFromExactlyOneGroupedTool` / `TestNoGroupedToolSpansTwoRiskClasses` — all pass.
- Full `go test ./internal/web/` — only failure is `Test_no_get_route_serves_a_null_on_empty_state` on `/api/issues/` (400 "Invalid issue ID"), **confirmed pre-existing on clean HEAD** (stashed my changes, same failure).
- Live smoke against the bench DB: `/ui2/history` 200 (35 KB, 4.5 ms), `?search=login` 200 (9.2 KB), `/ui2/history/780` 200, `/ui2/issues` 200 (14.6 KB, 394 findings, severity counts rendered), `/ui2/issues/1` 200, assets 200, old `/` and `/app.js` unchanged. Browser pass via agent-browser: DCL 269 ms, 100 rows rendered, 941 DOM nodes, click-through to detail pane works, screenshots in `/tmp/ui-fw/shot-ui2-*.png`.

## 5. Summary — what was built, numbers, what's next

**Built:** a server-rendered `/ui2/` console (stdlib templates + vendored htmx+SSE) with end-to-end History (server-paged, DSL filter, substring search, infinite scroll, request/response detail) and Issues (grouped, severity-counted, evidence in detail), live-refresh via the existing `/api/events` SSE hub, served alongside the untouched React SPA.

**Numbers vs old UI (same bench data):** 3.0 MB → 89 KB first load; 226 KB history JSON → 35 KB HTML page (100 rows, server-paged); 1.1 MB issues JSON → 14.6 KB grouped HTML; detail 2 JSON calls → 1.4 KB HTML.

**Not verified / known gaps:**
- On this tree, restored projects serve `request: null` for every exchange (the `ex.Request = core.MsgPtr(...)` line present in commit e2cda670 is absent from HEAD's `LoadExchanges`; the DB column is populated). /ui2/ renders an explicit note instead of a blank pane; fixing the restore wiring is a separate pre-existing bug, not part of this slice.
- `internal/mcp` screenshot test fails for a missing `ui/node_modules` in this environment — pre-existing, unrelated.
- The old UI's `bun run check` was not run (no `node_modules` in this worktree); the regenerated TS files were produced by the repo's own generators and the Go-side contract tests pass.
- Only History and Issues were sliced; Intercept/Scanner/Scope/Target pages are the next pages in the migration plan (each is one template + one handler + one manifest entry, per this slice's pattern).

## 6. Load test — 2k events/sec (added after the first slice)

In-process harness (`internal/web/ui2_load_test.go`, 5 tests, all passing): 20k seeded
exchanges (each firing a `changeHistory` notify through the store observer), while a goroutine
floods `live.notify(changeHistory)` at 2000/sec, while 1200 requests hit 6 ui2 paths:

| Measurement | p50 | p90 | p99 | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/ui2/history` (+filter/search/offset/issues variants) under flood, 20k rows | 5.6 ms | 15.1 ms | 31.8 ms | 53.0 ms |
| Detail pane (`/ui2/history/{id}`, reads message bytes) under flood | 16.7 µs | — | 73.7 µs | 225 µs |
| Filter typing (growing `search=` prefixes, 60 requests) | 9.7 ms | — | 24.9 ms | 26.6 ms |
| Old SPA catch-all `/` under flood | 1.9 µs | — | 31.7 µs | — |

SSE coalescing under flood: 2000 notifies/sec → **6.7 frames/sec** (the hub's 150 ms window
ceiling), carrying every one of ~2950 notifies exactly once (Swap-claim in `flush`). The
browser's re-fetch loop is therefore capped at ~7 refreshes/sec no matter how hard the
capture path fires — the property that keeps the tab responsive during a saturated crawl.

Live browser pass under a background load generator (~470–520 req/s hammering
`/api/history`, `/api/issues`, `/api/dashboard`, `/api/stats`, `/api/events/stats`,
`/api/scope` — read-only, no proxy traffic): `/ui2/history` answered 200 in 6.9 ms;
first load DCL 238 ms with 3 resources (htmx 50 KB, sse 4 KB, app.js 2 KB); heap 13 MB;
942 DOM nodes. Infinite scroll drove 100 → 200 → 300 → 400 → 401 rows with exactly one
live sentinel at all times (older sentinels removed after each swap), each page fetch ~19 ms.
Filter `path~rest` narrowed 783 → 103 rows; `path~rest` + `search=login` → 16 rows; URL
carries the state (`?q=…&search=…`), so filtered views are bookmarkable. Row click updates
the detail pane and marks the row selected; issue occurrence rows deep-link into history
detail. DSL syntax note: `path:` is not valid — the operator uses `path~x` / `path=x`
(the API's own error text names the valid operators; /ui2/ shows it inline).

## 7. UX audit — /ui2/ vs old SPA

Driven with agent-browser against the bench DB (screenshots in `/tmp/ui-fw/shot-ui2-*.png`):

| Aspect | Old SPA | /ui2/ | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| First paint | 2.7 MB JS parse before anything | 56 KB JS + server-rendered HTML, DCL ~240 ms | **ui2 wins** |
| History under 783 rows | 500-row JSON page + virtualizer, 1,835 DOM nodes | 100 rows/page server-paged, 942 DOM nodes, infinite scroll works | **ui2 wins** |
| Filter/search | client-side over the loaded page; URL state via hash | server-side `q` DSL + `search`, state in the query string (shareable URL) | **ui2 wins** |
| Detail pane | 2 JSON fetches, blank request pane on restored projects | 1 HTML fragment; explicit "No request bytes recorded" note | **ui2 wins** (honesty) |
| Issues | 1.1 MB full JSON for evidence; tree from 215 KB summary | 14 KB grouped list, evidence in per-issue detail, occurrences deep-link to history | **ui2 wins** |
| Live updates | SSE + 350 ms debounce + React re-render of the whole list | SSE → htmx fragment swap of just `#rows` (≤7/s coalesced) | **ui2 wins** (smaller DOM churn) |
| Empty state | — | "0 of 783 rows · search zzzznomatch · page 0–0" + "No rows match." row | ok |
| a11y basics | Radix landmarks, WCAG-tagged live pass | `header`/`nav`/`main` landmarks, `role=region` panes, `aria-live=polite` detail, `aria-label` on both filter inputs, `scope=col` on all `th`, `lang=en`, no images-without-alt, no empty links | ok (basic pass done; full axe run not done — no node_modules here) |
| Console errors | — | none observed during the whole driven session | ok |
| Keyboard | old SPA has hotkeys (Ctrl+R etc.) | **/ui2/ has none yet** — gap, listed below | old UI wins |
| Multi-select rows, send-to tools, context menus | present in old SPA | **absent in /ui2/** — gap | old UI wins |
| Dark mode | theme toggle | `prefers-color-scheme` only, no manual toggle | old UI wins |
| Intercept / Scanner / Scope / Target / Repeater pages | full | **not in the slice** | old UI wins |

**Honest gaps of the slice:** no keyboard shortcuts, no row multi-select/actions, no manual
theme toggle, only History + Issues exist. These are the next migration pages, not defects
of the chosen approach — each is one template + one handler + one manifest entry.

## 8. Bugs found while testing (fixed in this branch)

1. **Infinite scroll stalled after page 1**: the sentinel's `hx-swap="outerHTML"` on `#rows`
   replaced the whole block, and every appended page re-added a sentinel with the same id, so
   only the first ever fired. Fixed: append mode (`offset` present + `HX-Request`) emits
   rows-only via `history_rows_append.html` with `hx-swap="beforeend"` on `#rows-body`, and
   `app.js` removes all but the newest `.sentinel-row` after each swap. Pinned by
   `TestUI2HistoryAppendFragmentIsRowsOnly`.
2. **`html/template` choked on inline JS**: the layout's `<script>` block ended in a JS
   regex/brace context the template parser reads as non-text. Fixed by moving all client JS
   to a static `/ui2/app.js` (also a new asset route + manifest entry).
3. **a11y**: added landmark roles, `aria-label`s, `scope=col`, `aria-live` on the detail pane.

## 9. Full migration (second commit, b124f82d) — all 18 tool pages in /ui2/

Every old-UI tool now has a server-rendered page under /ui2/, sharing one nav partial and the
same SSE live-refresh: Dashboard, Site map, Scope, Intercept (+ enable/disable/forward-all/
drop-all actions), HTTP History, Issues, WebSockets, Proxy settings (listeners, options,
match&replace, passthrough), Repeater (editor + send through /api/repeater/send), Decoder
(decode/encode/hash), Comparer, Logger (server-paged, infinite scroll), Organizer, Session,
Extensions, Scanner (configs, BCheck corpus, coverage, live-audit, queue), Issue definitions,
Settings overview. Each page reuses the existing JSON handler's own view builder server-side,
so ui2 and the JSON API cannot drift. 24 Go tests cover every page (shell+fragment, markers,
nav completeness, decoder md5, comparer diff, intercept actions, 405s).

**UAT (agent-browser against the bench DB, all live):** all 18 pages answer 200 with the shell
(4.6–41 KB each, 2–51 ms); nav has 19 links; dashboard shows "783 exchanges · 1829 messages ·
13453497 bytes · suite running"; sitemap renders 190 nodes; history infinite-scroll 100→201
rows with one live sentinel, `status=403` filter narrows 783→24, row click fills the detail
pane and marks the row selected; decoder run returns md5("hello") correctly; comparer renders
a diff. 17 screenshots + a 17 s walkthrough video + overview grid were emailed to
awayt3005@proton.me via proton-cli (message in Sent, 2026-10-30).

**Remaining honest gaps (old SPA still wins these):** keyboard shortcuts, row multi-select /
send-to-tool actions, manual theme toggle, Intruder attack launch UI, Collaborator/Sequencer/
content-discovery/DOM-auditor/authz interactive flows, and per-row edit forms (intercept edit,
organizer notes, scope rule editor). Each is one template + one form handler + one manifest
entry following the established pattern; the read-only surfaces are all migrated.

web-package failure remains the pre-existing `/api/issues/` nil-slice one confirmed on HEAD.

<!-- Generated: 2026-07-28 | Updated: 2026-09-04 -->

# burpsy

## Purpose

A memory-frugal HTTP testing proxy with a web UI. It exists to run PortSwigger's published BCheck
corpus — unmodified and honestly counted — against real traffic without the memory cost that forces
Burp to discard scan work.

The whole architecture follows from one thesis: **raw bytes are written once and never copied.**
Everything downstream (history rows, insertion points, attack results, findings) holds a message id
plus `(offset, len)` spans. Burp's audit engine bounds cost by *discarding* work (`LIMIT_EXCEEDED`)
because `requests × insertion points × checks` is unbounded when each of those is a materialised
object. Here the resident set does not scale with work in flight, so the cap becomes backpressure
rather than dropped findings.

## Two trees: which one to work in

This repository holds **two implementations of burpsy**, and the distinction is the first thing to
get right:

| Tree | Language | Status | Work here? |
|------|----------|--------|------------|
| `burpsy-go/` | Go (module `github.com/burpsy-go/burpsy`) | **The active implementation.** All new feature work, the shipping binary, and the React web UI live here | **Yes — this is where changes land** |
| `crates/` | Rust (Cargo workspace, 13 crates) | **Frozen reference.** The original implementation, kept as the parity oracle the Go port is measured against | Read for behaviour and design intent; do not build new features here |

The Go port is measured against the Rust reference in `burpsy-go/gaps.md` — a source-verified ledger of
every known Rust↔Go difference. When behaviour is ambiguous, the Rust crate is the specification and
the Go package is the thing being made to match it. **Do not "fix" the Rust tree to track the Go one**;
it is deliberately frozen so it stays a stable oracle.

Because both trees exist side by side, be explicit about which one a path belongs to: `crates/scanner`
is Rust, `burpsy-go/internal/scanner` is Go, and they are different code with the same job.

## Key Files

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `burpsy-go/` | **The Go implementation — the primary tree.** See `burpsy-go/AGENTS.md` |
| `crates/` | The Rust reference implementation, frozen (see `crates/AGENTS.md`) |
| `Cargo.toml` | Rust workspace manifest. Edition 2024, resolver 3, thirteen member crates |
| `verify.sh` | The Rust gate: build with zero warnings, clippy, unit tests, BCheck corpus conformance, e2e suites. `QUICK=1` skips e2e |
| `e2e-go.sh` | End-to-end smoke test that runs the **Go** binary — the Go analogue of `e2e.sh`, ports offset by 100 so the two suites cannot collide. CI runs it nightly (`.github/workflows/nightly.yml`), not per merge |
| `ui-live.sh` | **The UI gate — manual; no CI runs it.** Boots the real console, seeded, and prints the live browser pass an agent drives with `agent-browser` (see `burpsy-go/docs/UI-VERIFICATION.md`) |
| `e2e-ui.sh` | Playwright suite for the React web UI. Still runnable, no longer the gate — see `burpsy-go/docs/UI-VERIFICATION.md` for why |
| `ROADMAP.md` | Top-level feature roadmap / Burp teardown reference (the working plan lives in `.planning/`) |
| `docs/DEVELOPMENT-PROCESS.md` | How work lands: rounds, test tiers (what CI runs, what is nightly, what is manual), review, beads closure. Wins over older instructions |
| `scripts/` | Process tooling: `affected-go-tests.sh` (T1/T2 test set), `beads-lint.py` and `review-gate.sh` (CI checks), `beads-close-merged.py` (round closures), `dev-setup.sh` (once per clone) |
| `DESIGN.md` | The design-system contract between the Figma source and the React UI in `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/` |
| `serve.sh`, `integrate.sh` | Launch / integration harness for the Rust tree |
| `e2e.sh`, `e2e-audit.sh`, `e2e-intercept.sh`, `e2e-scan.sh`, `e2e-tls.sh` | Rust end-to-end suites, driven by `verify.sh` unless `QUICK=1` |

## Subdirectories

| Directory | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `burpsy-go/` | The Go implementation: `cmd/` binaries, `internal/` packages, `docs/`, and the React UI under `internal/web/ui/` (see `burpsy-go/AGENTS.md`) |
| `crates/` | The thirteen Rust reference crates (see `crates/AGENTS.md`) |
| `docs/` | Rust-side reverse-engineering and protocol research notes (see `docs/AGENTS.md`). Go-side docs live in `burpsy-go/docs/` |
| `.planning/` | GSD planning state — roadmap, requirements, per-phase context/plans/research. Not code; read it to understand *why* something is being built. Authored against the Rust tree; the Go port's live status lives in `burpsy-go/PORT_STATUS.md`, `burpsy-go/gaps.md`, and the dated `burpsy-go/docs/HANDOFF-*.md` |
| `.omc/`, `.superpowers/`, `.codebase-memory/` | Operational agent state. Gitignored or machine-generated; never edit by hand |

### Where AGENTS.md files live

There are two hierarchies, one per tree:

- **Rust** — one `AGENTS.md` per meaningful unit: this root, `crates/`, each of the thirteen crates,
  `docs/`, and two nested directories that carry their own rules (`crates/web/src/routes/`,
  `crates/sender/src/transport/`). There is deliberately **no** `AGENTS.md` in `crates/*/src/` — a
  crate's `src/` *is* the crate — nor in the single-purpose directories. Those gaps are the design;
  do not fill them with boilerplate.
- **Go** — `burpsy-go/AGENTS.md` at the tree root, `burpsy-go/cmd/AGENTS.md`, `burpsy-go/internal/AGENTS.md`
  as the package index, and one `AGENTS.md` per meaningful `internal/` package. The trivial
  single-file helper packages (`internal/httputil`, `internal/toollog`) are covered by
  `internal/AGENTS.md` rather than carrying their own — same "one per meaningful unit, don't dilute"
  rule as the Rust side.

## For AI Agents

### Working In This Directory

- **Default to the Go tree.** Unless a task is explicitly about the Rust reference, new work goes in
  `burpsy-go/`. Check `burpsy-go/gaps.md` before assuming a capability is missing — it may already be
  ported.
- **How work lands — rounds, test tiers, review, beads closure — is `docs/DEVELOPMENT-PROCESS.md`.**
  Where an instruction here disagrees with it, it wins.
- **The Go gate, honestly stated.** What CI runs on every PR into master and every master push
  (T3, `.github/workflows/go.yml`): `gofmt -l .`, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` on the whole
  module; `go test ./... -count=1` and `go test -race ./internal/web/` — in full on a push to master,
  and on a PR only for the packages `scripts/affected-go-tests.sh` selects (in full when the PR
  touches go.mod/go.sum, CI files or testdata); and for the console `bun run check`, `bun run build`
  and a bundle-freshness check. A docs/.beads/bench-only change runs none of the Go or console jobs.
  What runs only nightly (`.github/workflows/nightly.yml`): `e2e-go.sh`, and `-race` on every other
  package, `internal/scanner` and `internal/extscan` included. What no CI runs:
  the live browser pass for a console change (`./ui-live.sh`, then
  `burpsy-go/docs/UI-VERIFICATION.md`) — that one is yours to do and report; Playwright is no longer
  the UI gate. Before reporting, run the affected-package tier (T1 in the process doc). The Rust
  gate is `verify.sh`. Do not declare work complete without the tier you owe, and say which ran.
- **Commit messages here are unusually substantive** — they explain why a change is right and what
  the obvious alternative gets wrong. Match that; a one-line summary will look out of place.
- Never commit CA material or keys, and never commit compiled binaries (a 13 MB `crawl-scan-demo`
  and the 33 MB `burpsy-go/burpsy` binary have both been staged by mistake). `.gitignore` already
  excludes CA material, `*.pem`, `*.key`, and the build outputs.
- The project's stated value is **honest counting**. Coverage numbers, skipped checks and
  unverifiable results are reported, never hidden. Code — or a doc — that makes a partial result look
  complete is a defect here even when the tests pass. This is why coverage figures are stated as
  *parse conformance* vs *runtime coverage* separately, and why a single headline number is not
  published until Security Research (CS-11) re-verifies it.

### Testing Requirements

Go (the active tree). Tiers are defined in `docs/DEVELOPMENT-PROCESS.md` section 4:

```bash
# T1, before reporting (you): the changed packages and everything whose tests import them
pkgs=$(scripts/affected-go-tests.sh origin/master)
cd burpsy-go
gofmt -l .                     # must print nothing
go vet ./...                   # must be clean
[ -n "$pkgs" ] && ../scripts/capped-run.sh -- go test -count=1 -timeout 30m $pkgs   # heavy runs are capped

# T3, CI on every PR into master and every master push (.github/workflows/go.yml; `gate` aggregates
# `changes`, `lint` and the `test` shard matrix). The shards together are the whole suite plus the
# internal/web race run (a PR runs only its affected part); reproduce one red shard locally with
# (prefix CI_AFFECTED_BASE=origin/master to reproduce a PR's affected-mode shard):
../scripts/capped-run.sh -- ../scripts/ci-shard.sh <shard>   # ../scripts/ci-shard.sh all lists them

# Nightly only (.github/workflows/nightly.yml) — not run per merge
../e2e-go.sh                   # end-to-end against the Go binary
```

A missing capability fails a package; it does not skip it green. Tests that need something the
machine may lack skip with a counted reason, and the package then fails unless the matching escape
hatch says the reduced run is deliberate. CI sets none of these:

- `BURPSY_ALLOW_NO_CHROME=1`: browser-driving packages (domexec, dominvader, blindxss, browser,
  crawler, scanner, web) pass with their Chrome tests skipped, listing them on stderr. The ledger is
  `burpsy-go/internal/domexec/domexectest`; Playwright's Chromium works if it is on PATH as `chromium`.
- `BURPSY_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_COVERAGE=1`: `internal/scanner`'s runtime coverage pin accepts rows
  skipped for a missing capability.
- `BURPSY_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_EXTSCAN=1`: `internal/extscan` and `internal/web`'s discovery tests pass
  without ffuf, nuclei or the template corpus.

UI changes (anything under `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/`): CI's `ui` job runs `bun run check`,
`bun run build` and fails when the committed bundle differs from a fresh build; run `bun run check`
yourself first (T1). The live browser pass is manual — no CI runs it:

```bash
./ui-live.sh                   # boot the real console, seeded, and print the pass
                               # ... drive it with agent-browser, then ./ui-live.sh --stop
                               # what the pass must cover: burpsy-go/docs/UI-VERIFICATION.md
```

Rust (the frozen reference):

```bash
cargo test --workspace          # ~1032 tests
cargo build --workspace         # must produce ZERO warnings
QUICK=1 ./verify.sh             # full gate minus e2e
./verify.sh                     # everything
```

### Known environment gotcha: clippy toolchain mismatch (Rust only)

This machine has **two Rust installations**. `/usr/bin/cargo` and `/usr/bin/rustc` are Debian
packages at 1.92.0 and win on `PATH`; `cargo-clippy` and `clippy-driver` exist only under rustup
(currently 1.95). Running plain `cargo clippy` mixes them and every crate fails with `E0514`. Use
`verify.sh`, which invokes clippy through rustup's own `cargo`, pins `RUSTC`, and gives clippy its own
`CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. A `rust-toolchain.toml` would not fix it — `/usr/bin/cargo` ignores it. This
affects only the Rust tree; the Go toolchain has no such split.

### Common Patterns (shared by both trees)

- **Doc comments explain *why*, including what the previous implementation got wrong.** See
  `crates/core/src/lib.rs`'s "The one invariant" or `burpsy-go/docs/DATA-MODEL.md`'s identity-hazard
  section (two dense id spaces that both count from zero).
- **Tests are named as full sentences that state a claim** and assert messages that say what a
  failure *means* rather than restating the comparison.
- **Invariants are made checkable, not asserted in prose** — `verify_index` / `VerifyIndex` both
  return the first disagreement they find and name the id.
- Refuse-by-default on unparseable input. A request whose path cannot be read is refused, never
  waved through.

## Dependencies

### Rust — crate order (depend only downward)

```
core  ──►  bcheck  ──►  scanner  ──►  proxy  ──►  web  ──►  cli
  │           │                          ▲         ▲         ▲
  ├──────────►└──►  sender  ─────────────┴─────────┤         │
  ├──►  intruder  ───────────────────────────────► │         │
  └──►  tools  ──────────────────────────────────► │         │
```

Leaves added later, all real edges: `http2` (used by `sender`, `proxy`), `query` (used by `core`,
`tools`, `web`), `session` (depends on `core`; used by `web`), `sequencer` (depends on `core`,
`sender`; used by `web`). `proxy` dev-depends on `web` (dev-only cycle, so integration tests can
drive the real HTTP API).

### Go

The Go tree is a single module (`github.com/burpsy-go/burpsy`, `go 1.26`) whose packages live under
`internal/`. The dependency direction mirrors the Rust spine — `core` is the root every package
holds, `sender` is the one authorising path to a socket — but is enforced by Go's package graph
rather than by crate manifests. See `burpsy-go/internal/AGENTS.md` for the package map. Notable
external dependencies: `golang.org/x/net/http2`, `chromedp`/`cdproto` (headless DOM confirmation),
`dop251/goja` (JS execution), `PuerkitoBio/goquery`, `projectdiscovery/wappalyzergo`,
`modernc.org/sqlite` (pure-Go SQLite mirror), `mvdan.cc/sh` (the `run tool` shell substrate),
`go.uber.org/zap` (logging).

### External (Rust)

- `tokio` 1.x — async runtime · `bytes` 1.12 — refcounted zero-copy slices · `rustls` 0.23 /
  `tokio-rustls` 0.26 / `rcgen` — TLS · `axum` 0.8 — web API · `memmap2` 0.9, `crc32fast` 1.5 —
  sealed segment storage · `parking_lot`, `regex`, `serde`, `anyhow`, `tracing`.
